chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl narrated from Amr ibn Sa'id from al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the fasting person who smokes with a stick or otherwise, and the smoke enters his throat, so he said: 'It is permissible, there is no harm in it.' I asked him about the fasting person in whom dust enters his throat, he said: 'There is no harm.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it / it is valid

ai.seo_question: Does smoking or inhaling dust invalidate the fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the mere entry of smoke or dust into the throat does not break the fast, distinguishing between intentional ingestion and passive inhalation. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that minor, unavoidable particles do not nullify the state of fasting, provided they do not reach the stomach in significant quantity. This ruling is foundational for understanding the permissibility of various environmental factors during Ramadan.
